questions.prompt: Independent knowledge sources read/write a shared central dataset under a controller, solving opportunistically (no fixed sequence) — an expert-system domain. Which architectural style?
questions.explain: **Blackboard** signals: independent knowledge sources + shared central data + controller/mediator + opportunistic solving. Pipes-and-filters needs a fixed sequential transformation; client-server has no collaborative solving; layered is hierarchical separation.

questions.prompt: In Kruchten's 4+1, the LOGICAL view captures ______ and serves ______:
options: Functional structure (classes/components) · end users and analysts/designers
questions.explain: 4+1 map: **Logical** = functionality (Class/Component diagrams; end users) · **Process** = runtime concurrency (Sequence/Communication; integrators) · **Development** = code modules (Package; programmers/managers) · **Physical** = deployment (Deployment diagram; system engineers) · **+1 Scenarios** = use cases that tie and validate all four.

questions.prompt: Why are SCENARIOS the "+1" in the 4+1 view model?
options: They cut across and VALIDATE the other four views against required behavior
questions.explain: Each view isolates one stakeholder concern; **scenarios (use cases) tie the four views together** and prove the architecture supports the required behavior — relevant to all stakeholders, especially customers.

questions.prompt: Select THREE genuine architectural quality attributes (with their course definitions):
options: Modifiability — complexity of changing the system for current/future needs
Performance — capacity to do useful work under time/resource constraints
Interoperability — ability to collaborate with other systems
questions.explain: The slide list: usability, **modifiability**, security, **performance**, reliability, availability, portability, testability, **interoperability** — each with a one-line definition you should be able to quote.

questions.prompt: Select THREE documented activities/responsibilities of the software ARCHITECT:
options: Design major components and their interfaces
Evaluate and validate the architecture (long, iterative)
Write all the unit tests personally
questions.explain: Architect's activities: identify **stakeholder concerns**; select **architectural representations/views**; manage **influences of decisions**; design **major components + interfaces**; **evaluate/validate**; maintain **design synchronicity** (implementation reflects design).

questions.prompt: Millions of concurrent requests · teams must deploy services independently · a loyalty-module crash must not stop ride requests. Which architecture, and which requirement maps to 'fault isolation'?
options: Microservices — the loyalty-crash survival maps to fault isolation (separate service, core path keeps operating)
Monolith — crash survival via bigger servers
Layered — each layer is a team
Pipes and filters — crashes flow downstream
questions.explain: **Microservices**: horizontal independent scaling (millions of requests), **deployment independence** (pricing released without touching matching/payment — the defining criterion), **fault isolation** (loyalty is a separate service; matching + payment keep running). Sketch: API Gateway → RideRequest/Matching/Pricing/Payment/Loyalty services, each owning its data store.

questions.prompt: Data flows through a fixed series of independent transformation steps, each consuming the previous step's output (e.g., compiler stages). Which style?
questions.explain: **Pipes and filters** = fixed sequential transformations, each filter independent, connected by pipes. Contrast with blackboard (opportunistic, shared data) and event-driven (publish/subscribe on events).
